title: Daily Security Intelligence Briefing — September 07, 2026
summary: Active zero-day exploitation is hitting infrastructure management tools including N-able N-central, ConnectWise ScreenConnect, and MikroTik routers (BleepingComputer, SANS ISC). Organizations face immediate patching requirements for exposed management interfaces alongside newly disclosed endpoint zero-days (Infosecurity Magazine).

tier2.title: 1. N-able Emergency Hotfix 4 Issued for Critical N-central Zero-Day Under Active Exploitation

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Vulnerability Management / RMM Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: N-able released an emergency hotfix to address CVE-2026-86218, a maximum-severity pre-authenticated remote code execution vulnerability in its N-central remote monitoring platform. Active attacks in the wild prompted the release, affecting all on-premises builds prior to version 2026.3.1.14.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Pre-authenticated remote code execution allows unauthenticated attackers full control over N-central servers.; Requires immediate update to Hotfix 4 (build 2026.3.1.14) even for servers patched a day prior.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: N-able released an emergency hotfix for CVE-2026-86218, a remote code execution (RCE) flaw affecting N-central... that could allow for pre-authenticated remote code execution on the N-central server.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: BleepingComputer

tier2.title: 2. Unpatched ConnectWise ScreenConnect Zero-Day Exploited to Spread VBScript Malware

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Remote Access Security / Malware Operations

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: ConnectWise issued an urgent advisory warning of an unpatched file transfer vulnerability in ScreenConnect Remote Access. Attackers are abusing rogue client connections and diverse initial access vectors to deploy four-stage VBScript malware to newly connected hosts.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Vulnerability impacts both cloud and on-premise deployments with an official CVE and patch pending.; Temporary mitigations must be applied immediately to restrict unauthorized file transfer capabilities.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: A file transfer flaw in ScreenConnect Remote Access Support and Access sessions affects both Cloud and On-Premise deployments, ConnectWise confirmed.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: BleepingComputer

tier2.title: 3. Active Exploitation of MikroTik RouterOS SSH Authentication Bypass Flaws

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Network Infrastructure / Router Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Threat actors are actively exploiting a chain of vulnerabilities in MikroTik RouterOS targeting exposed SSH interfaces. Attackers gain administrative access and create rogue local accounts on compromised routers to maintain persistence.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Organizations with internet-exposed RouterOS SSH management interfaces must assume compromise.; Patches are available, but administrators must inspect user databases for unauthorized administrative accounts.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: The vulnerability allows an SSH authentication bypass and is already being exploited. At this point, assume compromise.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: SANS Internet Storm Center

tier2.title: 4. Researcher Publishes Privilege Escalation Zero-Day Exploit for CrowdStrike Falcon

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Endpoint Security / Zero-Day Disclosures

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: A security researcher publicly disclosed a working zero-day local privilege escalation vulnerability affecting CrowdStrike Falcon endpoint agents. If executed on a host, an attacker with low privilege can elevate rights on the system.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Requires prior local code execution access on the target endpoint to trigger.; Highlights security risks inherent to privileged kernel-level security agents.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: A security researcher has posted a zero-day exploit in CrowdStrike which could allow hackers to escalate privileges.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: Infosecurity Magazine

tier2.title: 5. French Legal Sector Targeted in €35 Million Business Email Compromise Operation

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Threat Intelligence / Cybercrime

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: A major Business Email Compromise (BEC) campaign successfully siphoned €35 million from French notary firms. Attackers compromised legitimate communications to manipulate high-value wire transfers.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Illustrates extreme financial risk targeting specialized legal and financial processing sectors.; Mandates strict out-of-band verification procedures for high-value financial transactions.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Hackers steal €35 million euros from French notaries, OpenAI agents hacked a German wiki...

fields.label: Source
fields.value: Risky Business
